ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaussian reward head trained with a pairwise likelihood
PROPOSAL: Replace the scalar value head of a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct reward model with a head that outputs a mean and a log-variance, and train it on 30000 pairs of HelpSteer2-Preference with the probability that the chosen response beats the rejected one computed from the two Gaussians. Evaluate ranking accuracy on RewardBench, and calibration of predicted pairwise probabilities with expected calibration error and reliability curves on a 2000-pair held-out split. Check whether predicted variance rises on pairs where annotators disagree.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry scalar model trained on the same pairs; the Gaussian head with variance fixed to 1; temperature scaling applied after training to the scalar model; 3 seeds for each variant.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Ranking accuracy should stay within one point of the scalar baseline while expected calibration error falls by a third. Predicted variance may correlate only weakly with disagreement, since few pairs in the training set carry conflicting labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture-of-Gaussians reward heads with ensembles for uncertainty
PROPOSAL: Train a reward model on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B with heads that output a mixture of Gaussians, tuning the number of components, and draw 90000 pairs from HelpSteer2-Preference, UltraFeedback and Skywork-Reward-Preference. Build deep ensembles for each setting, and retrain each member on resampled data. Report the correlation of predicted variance with the number of annotators who disagreed on each pair. Evaluate ranking accuracy on RewardBench and RM-Bench, calibration with expected calibration error on 6000 held-out pairs, and the annotated subsets.
CONTROLS: a Bradley-Terry scalar model trained on the same pairs for each base; temperature scaling; Monte Carlo dropout; 3 seeds for each variant.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Ranking accuracy should stay within one point of scalar baselines while expected calibration error falls by a third. Ensembles may match mixtures on calibration at much greater training volume.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Absolute quality anchoring with 500 pointwise labels
PROPOSAL: Ground a pairwise-trained reward model on an absolute scale using few quality annotations. Start from a Skywork-Reward-style Llama-3.1-8B model, freeze the backbone, and fit a monotone mapping from reward to a graded quality level on 500 annotated responses from HelpSteer2 using ordinal regression with a learned threshold set. Then fine-tune the whole model jointly with the pairwise loss and an ordinal loss on the same labels. Evaluate on 3000 held-out annotated responses and on RewardBench, reporting quality-level accuracy, expected calibration error and ranking accuracy.
CONTROLS: The unanchored model with a single global threshold chosen on the labels; isotonic regression on frozen scores; the joint model with the ordinal loss weight set to 0; 3 seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Frozen anchoring should give most of the calibration gain, and joint training should add about 2 points of quality-level accuracy at a cost of under half a point of ranking accuracy. The thresholds may not carry over to responses from other generators.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchoring reward scales with pointwise labels at graded annotation sizes
PROPOSAL: Ground a pairwise-trained reward model on an absolute scale using quality annotations of growing size, up to 2000 responses from HelpSteer2 and UltraFeedback. For Llama-3.1-8B, fit frozen ordinal mappings, then fine-tune jointly with the pairwise and ordinal losses over a grid of loss weights with 3 seeds. Evaluate on 6000 held-out annotated responses and on RewardBench, RM-Bench and JudgeBench, reporting quality-level accuracy, expected calibration error and ranking accuracy at each annotation size, and rank correlation between anchored scores and pointwise ratings, with a plot of calibration error against label count.
CONTROLS: An unanchored model with a single global threshold chosen on the labels; isotonic regression on frozen scores; the joint model with the ordinal loss weight set to 0; a prompted judge giving pointwise scores.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Calibration should improve quickly up to 500 labels and level off, with joint training adding about 2 points of quality-level accuracy at small ranking cost. Thresholds may not transfer to responses from other generators.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modelling annotator disagreement with per-annotator rating distributions
PROPOSAL: Use the per-annotator attribute ratings of HelpSteer2 to train a reward model on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct that predicts the full distribution of ratings, parameterised as a categorical over 5 levels for each of 5 attributes, and derives pairwise preference probabilities from the distributions. Evaluate agreement with held-out majority preferences on 3000 pairs, calibration of the preference probability, and whether the entropy of predicted ratings separates the 20% of pairs with lowest annotator agreement from the rest by AUROC.
CONTROLS: A scalar regression model on mean ratings; a categorical head trained on majority labels only, without disagreement signal; a shuffled-annotator version that destroys the disagreement structure; 3 seeds for each model.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Entropy should separate low-agreement pairs with AUROC near 0.65, and calibration should improve over the scalar model. Disagreement in the dataset may reflect annotation noise rather than genuine ambiguity, which would limit what the head can learn.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distributional reward model trained on disagreement from many datasets
PROPOSAL: Train a reward model on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct that predicts full rating distributions for the attributes of HelpSteer2, then extend training with preference votes from UltraFeedback, Chatbot Arena, Skywork-Reward-Preference, PKU-SafeRLHF, Nectar and Anthropic HH. Evaluate agreement with held-out majority preferences on 12000 pairs, calibration, and AUROC of rating entropy for the 20% lowest-agreement pairs, repeating each run for 3 seeds, and compare predicted entropy with the spread of raw annotator ratings.
CONTROLS: Scalar regression on mean ratings; categorical heads trained on majority labels only; a shuffled-annotator version; a Bradley-Terry model for each dataset; 3 seeds for each model.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Entropy should separate low-agreement pairs with AUROC near 0.65 and improve calibration over the scalar model. Disagreement may reflect annotation noise rather than genuine ambiguity, which would limit gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixed acceptance threshold on absolute reward scores
PROPOSAL: Test whether one fixed threshold on a calibrated reward separates good from bad responses in other domains. Take a reward model trained with an ordinal quality head on Llama-3.1-8B, pick the threshold that maximises F1 on 1500 chat responses from HelpSteer2, and apply it unchanged to 1500 responses each from math (MATH solutions with correctness labels), code (HumanEval completions with test outcomes) and safety (BeaverTails). Report precision, recall and F1 at the fixed threshold and at the per-domain optimum.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry scalar model with the same threshold procedure; a prompted judge giving pointwise grades; a threshold picked on the pooled data; bootstrap intervals over responses.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The calibrated model should lose less than 5 F1 points when moving from the tuned domain to the others, while the scalar model should lose more than 15. Safety may remain the hardest domain because refusals and harmless answers are scored alike.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-domain fixed thresholds for calibrated reward scores in eight domains
PROPOSAL: Test whether one fixed threshold on a calibrated reward separates good from bad responses in eight domains. Take an ordinal-head reward model on Gemma-2-9B, pick the threshold that maximises F1 on 3000 chat responses, and apply it unchanged to 3000 responses each from MATH, GSM8K, HumanEval, MBPP, BeaverTails, XSTest, role-play dialogue and long-form question answering. Report precision, recall and F1 at the fixed threshold and at each per-domain optimum, for 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry scalar model with the same threshold procedure; a prompted judge giving pointwise grades; thresholds picked on pooled data; bootstrap intervals over responses.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: A calibrated model should lose under 5 F1 points when the threshold moves to other domains, a scalar one more than 15. Safety may remain the hardest domain because refusals and harmless answers are scored alike.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-aware Best-of-N selection on mathematical reasoning
PROPOSAL: Use a reward model with predicted mean and variance to select among N sampled solutions, ranking by a lower confidence bound mean minus lambda times standard deviation. Sample N of 4, 16 and 64 solutions per problem from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on 1500 MATH problems and 1000 GSM8K problems at a fixed temperature, and compare selection by mean, by lower bound with two values of lambda, and by majority vote. Report accuracy of the selected solution and the rate at which low-confidence selections are wrong.
CONTROLS: Random selection; selection by the mean of a Bradley-Terry scalar model; majority voting; an oracle with access to the final answer; 3 seeds for sampling.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The lower bound should add 1 to 2 points over the mean at N of 64 by avoiding confidently wrong selections, with no gain at N of 4. Gains may be absorbed by majority voting on easy problems.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Best-of-N selection rules with reward uncertainty at growing sample sizes
PROPOSAL: Use a reward model with predicted mean and variance to select among N sampled solutions, with N growing from 2 to 256, drawing from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on MATH, GSM8K, AIME, HumanEval and MBPP, at 3 temperatures. Compare selection by mean, by lower bound with a ladder of lambda values, by Thompson draws, and by majority vote. Report accuracy of the selected solution and the rate of wrong low-confidence picks, with 5 sampling seeds and bootstrap intervals over problems.
CONTROLS: Random selection; mean selection from a Bradley-Terry scalar model; majority voting; an oracle with access to the final answer.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The lower bound should add 1 to 2 points over the mean at N of 64 and give no gain at N of 4. Majority voting may absorb the gains on easy problems.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quality-level head with a short critique before the score
PROPOSAL: Add a brief natural-language critique of at most 60 tokens before the scalar read-out of a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct reward model, with the critique generated by the model itself under supervised fine-tuning on 8000 HelpSteer2 rationales built from the attribute ratings. Compare ranking accuracy on RewardBench and calibration on 1000 held-out responses against the same model without critique, with and without the critique text fed to the score head.
CONTROLS: A direct scalar head with no critique; a model whose critique is replaced by a random critique from another response; a critique-only judge with no score head; 2 seeds.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Critique should raise accuracy by about one point on reasoning and chat subsets and improve calibration slightly, while the random-critique control should drop below the direct model. The critique may add latency without helping on safety prompts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Critique-then-score reward model for critique lengths and data sources
PROPOSAL: Add natural-language critiques of graded length before the scalar read-out of a reward model built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with critiques produced under supervised fine-tuning on 40000 rationales drawn from HelpSteer2, UltraFeedback and synthetic critiques from a stronger judge. Compare ranking accuracy on RewardBench, RM-Bench and JudgeBench, and calibration on 5000 held-out responses, against the same model without critique, with 3 seeds. Report the effect of critique length on accuracy.
CONTROLS: A direct scalar head with no critique; a model whose critique is replaced by a random critique from another response; a critique-only judge with no score head; Bradley-Terry baselines on each base.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Critique should raise accuracy by about one point on reasoning and chat subsets and slightly improve calibration, while random critiques should fall below direct models. Latency may rise without benefit on safety prompts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ordinal bin classification against Bradley-Terry scoring
PROPOSAL: Train a reward model whose head outputs a probability over 10 ordered quality bins instead of one scalar, using a loss that combines a cumulative-link term on the pointwise labels of HelpSteer2 and an expected-score pairwise term on preference pairs, so that the expected bin gives the reward. Use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 60000 pairs and 6000 pointwise labels. Evaluate on RewardBench, RM-Bench, held-out pointwise accuracy and expected calibration error, with 3 seeds and a few learning rates.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry scalar model on the same pairs; a classification head trained on pointwise labels alone; the combined loss with the pairwise term removed; a variant with fewer bins.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The ordinal model should match scalar ranking accuracy within one point and improve calibration clearly, at some cost on pairs with small quality gaps. Training with the combined loss may be unstable at high learning rates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ordinal bin heads with bin number and mixing weight studied jointly
PROPOSAL: Train a reward model whose head outputs a probability over ordered quality bins, varying the number of bins from 5 to 40, with a cumulative-link loss on pointwise labels and an expected-score pairwise loss under a grid of mixing weights. Use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B, with 300000 pairs from several sources and 30000 pointwise labels. Evaluate on RewardBench, RM-Bench, JudgeBench, pointwise accuracy and expected calibration error, with 5 seeds and a sweep of learning rates.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry scalar model on the same pairs for each base; classification heads trained on pointwise labels alone; the combined loss with the pairwise term removed.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: An ordinal model should match scalar ranking accuracy within one point and improve calibration clearly, at some cost on pairs with small quality gaps. Combined-loss training may be unstable at high learning rates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness of distributional reward models to flipped preference labels
PROPOSAL: Corrupt 10%, 20% and 30% of the training pairs of HelpSteer2-Preference by swapping chosen and rejected responses, then train a Gaussian-head reward model and a scalar Bradley-Terry model on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for each corruption level. Evaluate ranking accuracy on RewardBench and a clean 2000-pair split, calibration, and whether predicted variance rises on the flipped training pairs when scored by the final model, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: The scalar model with label smoothing at 0.1; a model with a loss that drops the 10% highest-loss pairs; training on clean labels as the ceiling; random scores as the floor.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The Gaussian head should lose about half as much accuracy as the scalar model at 30% corruption, and variance on flipped pairs should be at least 1.5 times that on clean ones. Variance may stay flat if the model memorises flipped labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Noise robustness of reward models under three corruption types
PROPOSAL: Corrupt training pairs from HelpSteer2-Preference and UltraFeedback at rates from 5% to 40% by swapping labels, adding length-biased flips and sampling flips in proportion to annotator disagreement, then train Gaussian-head, mixture-head, ordinal-head and scalar Bradley-Terry baselines on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for each combination. Evaluate ranking accuracy on RewardBench and RM-Bench, calibration, and predicted variance on flipped pairs, with 3 seeds, and compare results on the clean split with those on the noisy split.
CONTROLS: A scalar model with label smoothing at 0.1; a loss that drops the 10% highest-loss pairs; training on clean labels as the ceiling; random scores as the floor.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The Gaussian head should lose about half as much accuracy as the scalar model at 30% corruption, and variance on flipped pairs should be at least 1.5 times that on clean ones. Variance may stay flat if flipped labels are memorised.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapting a calibrated reward model to role-play dialogue with limited labels
PROPOSAL: Adapt an ordinal-head reward model from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, trained on general chat preferences, to role-play dialogue using 400 quality-annotated responses and 4000 unlabelled preference pairs from a role-play corpus. Update only a low-rank adapter of rank 16 with a loss mixing the ordinal term on the 400 labels and the pairwise term on the pairs. Report ranking accuracy on 1500 held-out role-play pairs, quality-level accuracy on 1000 held-out responses, calibration, and forgetting on RewardBench chat and reasoning subsets, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: No adaptation; pairwise-only adaptation; ordinal-only adaptation on the 400 labels; full fine-tuning with the same loss; a prompted judge with 8 in-context examples.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The mixed loss should add about 4 points of quality-level accuracy over pairwise-only adaptation while keeping ranking accuracy within one point, and forgetting on RewardBench should stay under one point. With 400 labels the threshold set may overfit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain adaptation of calibrated reward models at graded label counts
PROPOSAL: Adapt an ordinal-head reward model from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B to role-play dialogue, legal advice, medical question answering and creative writing, using quality annotations from 50 up to 1600 responses and 20000 unlabelled preference pairs per domain. Update adapters of a few ranks with a mixed ordinal and pairwise loss. Report ranking accuracy, quality-level accuracy, calibration and forgetting on RewardBench subsets, with 3 seeds for each setting and a learning curve for each.
CONTROLS: No adaptation; pairwise-only adaptation; ordinal-only adaptation on the labels; full fine-tuning with the same loss; a prompted judge with 8 in-context examples.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Mixed loss should add about 4 points of quality-level accuracy over pairwise-only adaptation with ranking accuracy within one point, and forgetting should stay under one point. With the smallest label sets the threshold set may overfit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Order and batch invariance of multi-response scoring
PROPOSAL: Test whether a reward model that scores a set of responses jointly in one context stays consistent. Build a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct reward model that reads 1, 2, 4 or 8 candidate responses to a prompt in one sequence and outputs a score for each, trained on 20000 HelpSteer2 and UltraFeedback prompts with their sampled responses. Measure score change under random permutations of the candidates, agreement between joint and single-response scores by Spearman correlation, and Best-of-8 accuracy on 800 MATH problems.
CONTROLS: The same model scoring each response alone; a model trained with fixed candidate order; a Bradley-Terry scalar model; a pairwise generative judge applied in a knockout tournament; 3 seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Permutation shifts should stay under 0.05 on a standardised scale and joint-versus-single correlation above 0.9, with Best-of-8 accuracy within one point of single scoring. Long contexts with 8 candidates may degrade position consistency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint scoring consistency with growing candidate sets on five domains
PROPOSAL: Test whether a reward model that scores candidates jointly in one context stays consistent. Build a reward model on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct that read from 1 up to 16 candidate responses in one sequence and output a score for each, trained on 100000 prompts with sampled responses from five sources. Measure score change under 10 random permutations, agreement between joint and single-response scores by Spearman correlation, and Best-of-N accuracy on MATH, HumanEval, GSM8K, AlpacaEval and Arena-Hard, and record how often the top candidate changes under permutation.
CONTROLS: The same model scoring each response alone; a model trained with fixed candidate order; a Bradley-Terry scalar model; a pairwise generative judge applied in a knockout tournament; 3 seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Permutation shifts should stay under 0.05 on a standardised scale and joint-versus-single correlation above 0.9, with Best-of-N accuracy within one point of single scoring. Contexts with 16 candidates may degrade position consistency.
